title: Deep research report
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for answering a research question with a cited report: a framed question, a search plan that looks for evidence against the answer, sources collected through permitted access and screened with recorded reasons, claims with exact quotes and locators, a synthesis with every sentence labeled, an adversarial review by a different worker, and a report that states its limits and what was not searched; for understanding a question, not for choosing what to build.
boundaries: Permitted access only: official APIs and downloads, robots.txt and terms respected, no paywall bypass, and Facebook or Instagram content only through Meta's official research tools.
Exact quotes and a citation for every claim; no personal data.
A different worker reviews, and a person decides what is delivered.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for answering a research question with a cited report that states its limits

value.lets_workers: Answer one research question with a cited report: frame the question and what would change the answer, plan the search with queries against the likely answer, collect sources through permitted access, screen them with recorded reasons, extract claims with exact quotes and locators, synthesize with every sentence labeled, have a different worker try to break it, and write a report with its evidence against, its limits and what was not searched. A person decides what is delivered.
value.not_for: Choosing what to build or adopt. The prior art and alternatives pack surveys existing options for a build decision; this pack informs understanding.
value.worked_example: Synthetic: whether community fridges reduce household food waste, from three stand-in sources: five claims with exact quotes, a contradiction kept, a passing adversarial review that proposes one more counter search, and a report with low confidence and its limits.

nouns.title: Guardrail: quote exactly, with a locator
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Every claim carries an exact quote from its source, character for character, with a locator a reader can follow: the page, section or paragraph, and the words just before and after the quote. A quote that does not appear in the source as written is removed and extracted again, never repaired in place.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every quote appears in its source's retrieved text with its prefix and suffix, exactly once.

nouns.title: Guardrail: the search is on the record
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Record every database and site searched, every query with its date and result count, every source found and every screening decision with its reason. List what was not searched, and why.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every planned query appears in the source log with its date and count, the screening flow adds up, and the report names what was not searched.

nouns.title: Guardrail: look for evidence against the answer
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Plan searches meant to find evidence against the likely answer, report that evidence next to the evidence for it, and keep contradictions visible instead of averaging them away.
value.how_it_is_checked: The search plan has at least one counter query, and the report lists the evidence against its answer or says plainly that none was found.

nouns.title: Guardrail: label every sentence: source, synthesis or open
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Label every sentence of a synthesis or report: source when quoted claims state it directly, synthesis when it infers across claims, and open when it is unknown. Source and synthesis sentences cite their claims.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every report sentence has a label, and every source or synthesis sentence cites at least one claim that exists.

nouns.title: Permitted access to research sources
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: Use a source's official API or download when it offers one, and read its terms first.
arXiv's APIs: no more than one request every three seconds, on a single connection, across every machine the requester runs; link to abstract pages instead of serving e-prints.
Crossref's REST API: use filters and select only the fields needed instead of one request per DOI, cache results, and back off on HTTP 429.
Retractions: check every cited DOI against Crossref's retraction data, through the update-type:retraction filter or the Retraction Watch data it publishes, before relying on it.
Web pages: read robots.txt and the site's terms, and stop when either forbids automated reading.
Facebook and Instagram content only through Meta's official research tools, such as the Meta Content Library and API, under their access terms, and never by scraping.
Paywalled full text only through access the requester already holds; never bypass a paywall or share the text.
No logins and no personal data, unless the requester grants a login explicitly for a source it licenses.

nouns.title: Screening sources, with a flow that adds up
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: Write the inclusion and exclusion criteria into the search plan before screening, and screen against them only.
Remove duplicates by DOI, then by normalized title and year, and count them.
Screen in two passes, title and summary, then full text, and give every exclusion one reason from the fixed list.
Exclude retracted works from the evidence and list them in the report.
The flow adds up: identified equals duplicates plus screened; screened equals excluded at title plus assessed; assessed equals excluded at full text plus included.

nouns.title: Grading how strongly the evidence supports a claim
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

levels.strong: Several independent primary sources agree and none credibly contradicts them.
levels.moderate: One good primary source, or several secondary sources that agree.
levels.limited: One secondary source, or primary sources that disagree.

rules: Grade claims, not sources alone, and say why in one line.
Self-reported, non-randomized or unmeasured results cannot make a claim strong by themselves.
A preprint, a press release or a news report cannot make a claim strong by itself.
The grade is a reading aid for the person who decides, not a certification.

nouns.title: Template: one research question, its scope and what would change the answer

value.describes: a research question: the question, why it matters, its type, scope and definitions, what evidence would change the answer, and what is out of scope
rules: A question about what to build or adopt goes to the prior art and alternatives pack instead.

nouns.title: Template: where and how to search, including for evidence against the answer

value.describes: a search plan: each source with its access and terms, each query with its purpose, the date range, the inclusion and exclusion criteria, the stop rules, and what will not be searched and why
rules: At least one query has purpose counter.
Criteria are written before screening starts.

nouns.title: Template: every search run and every source found, with digests

value.describes: a source log: every query run with its source, date and result count, and every source found with its publisher, date, address, access, retrieval time, text digest, retraction check and license note
rules: text_sha256 is the digest of the retrieved text the quotes are checked against.

nouns.title: Template: every screening decision with its reason, and the flow counts

value.describes: a screening log: each source's decision at each stage with its reason, and flow counts that add up
rules: Every exclusion has a reason.
The flow adds up as the screening rules say.

nouns.title: Template: claims with exact quotes, locators, direction and strength

value.describes: a claim extract: each claim's source, a plain statement, the exact quote with the words around it and a locator, its type, whether it supports or contradicts the likely answer, and a graded strength
rules: Quotes are exact; statements are plain paraphrases.
Only included sources yield claims.

nouns.title: Template: the answer so far, every sentence labeled, contradictions kept

value.describes: a synthesis: the answer so far and its confidence, every sentence labeled source, synthesis or open with the claims it rests on, and the agreements, contradictions and gaps
rules: Source and synthesis sentences cite claims.
Contradictions are listed, not averaged away.

nouns.title: Template: a different worker's attempt to break the synthesis

value.describes: an adversarial review by a worker other than the author: quotes rechecked against the sources, unsupported or overreaching sentences, counter-evidence the search missed, and whether the synthesis passed
rules: passed is true only when every quote is found and no sentence is unsupported or overreaching.
Missed counter-evidence searches are proposed as follow-up verbs; they fail the review only when the plan had no counter query.

nouns.title: Template: the cited report, with the evidence against it and its limits

value.describes: a research report: the question, a short answer with its confidence, labeled findings with their claims, the evidence against the answer, the method and flow, the limits, what was not searched, and the sources
rules: Every finding is labeled; source and synthesis findings cite claims.
evidence_against says None found, with the counter queries, when none was found.

nouns.title: Checklist a person runs before a report is delivered
nouns.category_reason: A short checklist a person runs is part of the report's guardrails.

items: The question is about understanding something, not about what to build or adopt.
Every quote matches its source, and a different worker checked them.
The evidence against the answer sits next to the evidence for it.
Every sentence is labeled, and synthesis sentences do not pose as facts.
The limits and what was not searched are plain enough for a reader to weigh.
No personal data, and every source was read as its terms permit.

verbs.title: Frame the research question
verbs.summary: Turn a request into one research question with its type, scope, definitions and the evidence that would change the answer, and route a build or adopt decision to the prior art and alternatives pack.
verbs.outcome: A research question, or no_change with a pointer when it is a build decision.

slots.name: request
slots.description: Pin of the requester's question in their own words.

steps: Write one question a source could answer, with its scope and definitions.
List what evidence would change the answer.
End no_change when the request is a choice of what to build or adopt, and propose the prior art and alternatives pack's survey-existing verb.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.research-question's schema.
would_change_answer names at least one finding.
The question asks one thing.

verbs.title: Plan the search, including against the answer
verbs.summary: Plan where and how to search: each source with its access, terms and rate, each query with its purpose, the date range, the inclusion and exclusion criteria, the stop rules, and what will not be searched.
verbs.outcome: A search plan with at least one counter query.
steps: Name each source with its official access, terms and rate rule.
Write queries for the answer, against it, for definitions and for background.
Fix the inclusion and exclusion criteria and the stop rules before any search runs.
List the sources that will not be searched, and why.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.search-plan's schema.
At least one query has purpose counter.
Every source has a terms address and a rate rule.

verbs.title: Run the searches and collect sources
verbs.summary: Run every planned query through the permitted access of each source, record each run's date and result count, and log every source found with its retrieved text's digest and a retraction check.
network: Only the sources the search plan names, through their official APIs, downloads or pages as their terms and robots.txt permit, at each source's stated rate; no logins, paywall bypasses or personal data.
steps: Read each source's terms and robots.txt first, and skip any source that forbids the reading, recording why.
Run every query at the source's rate and record its date and result count.
Keep each retrieved text's SHA-256, and check every DOI against the retraction data.
Stop at the plan's stop rules.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.source-log's schema.
Every planned query appears in searched with a date and a result count.
Every source has the SHA-256 of its retrieved text.

verbs.title: Screen the sources against the criteria
verbs.summary: Screen every source against the plan's criteria in two passes, give every exclusion a reason from the fixed list, exclude retracted works, and keep flow counts that add up.

slots.name: search_plan
slots.description: Pin of the search plan, for its criteria.

steps: Remove duplicates and count them.
Screen titles and summaries, then full texts, against the written criteria only.
Record a reason for every exclusion, including every retraction.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.screening-log's schema.
The flow counts add up as the screening rules say.
Every exclusion has a reason from the fixed list.

verbs.title: Extract claims with exact quotes
verbs.summary: Extract each included source's claims with an exact quote, the words around it, a locator, the claim's type, its direction against the likely answer and a graded strength.
steps: Quote exactly, with about 30 characters before and after, and a page, section or paragraph.
Paraphrase each statement plainly, and grade its strength with a one-line reason.
Keep contradicting claims; leave out personal data.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.claim-extract's schema.
Every quote, with its prefix and suffix, appears exactly once in its source's retrieved text.
Every claim's source was included in screening.

verbs.title: Synthesize, labeling every sentence
verbs.summary: Draft the answer so far from the claims, labeling every sentence source, synthesis or open, citing the claims behind each, and keeping agreements, contradictions and gaps visible.
steps: Label every sentence, and cite claims for every source and synthesis sentence.
State contradictions with both claims instead of averaging them.
Set the confidence no higher than the strongest uncontradicted claims allow.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.synthesis's schema.
Every source or synthesis sentence cites at least one existing claim.
Every claim with direction contradicts appears in a sentence or a contradiction.

verbs.title: Try to break the synthesis (a different worker)
verbs.summary: A worker other than the author rechecks every quote against its source, looks for unsupported or overreaching sentences, and runs counter searches the plan missed, listing every problem.
verbs.outcome: An adversarial review that passes only with no problems.

steps: Recheck every quote, with its prefix and suffix, against the retrieved text.
List every sentence that its claims do not support, or that claims more than they show.
Run counter searches the plan missed and propose any that matter as follow-up verbs.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.adversarial-review's schema.
quotes_checked equals the number of claims.
